classification.difficultyReason: Identify two angles standing on a highlighted arc across six different circle configurations.

content.prompt: Name two angles subtended by the same arc $AC$ in these circles.

spec.description: Circle with centre B, radii BA and BC, chords AD and DC, and highlighted lower arc AC.
spec.mathematics: A, D and C lie on the circle. B is the centre. The highlighted arc AC subtends angles ABC and ADC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC$ is at the centre and $\angle ADC$ is at the circumference. Both stand on the highlighted arc $AC$.

spec.description: Four circumference points joined by AD, DC, AB and BC; lower arc AC highlighted.
spec.mathematics: Angles ADC and ABC both have endpoints A and C and vertices on the opposite arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: The arms of $\angle ADC$ and $\angle ABC$ join their vertices to $A$ and $C$, so both stand on the highlighted arc $AC$.

spec.description: Chords DC, DA, CB and AB with short upper-right arc CA highlighted.
spec.mathematics: Angles ABC and ADC stand on the same short arc AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: Both $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ADC$ have arms ending at $A$ and $C$ and stand on the highlighted arc $AC$.

spec.description: Centre F with AF and FC; chords AE, AB, BC and ED. ED crosses the radius FC away from F. Upper arc AC through D highlighted.
spec.mathematics: A, D, C, B and E lie on the circle. Angle AFC is central and angle ABC is at the circumference, both standing on the highlighted arc AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: $\angle AFC$ is at the centre and $\angle ABC$ is at the circumference. Both stand on the highlighted arc $AC$ through $D$.

spec.description: Six circumference points A, F, E, B, D and C with chords AB, AE, CE, CB, CD and DF; upper-left arc AC highlighted.
spec.mathematics: Angles AEC and ABC stand on the highlighted arc AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: The arms of $\angle AEC$ and $\angle ABC$ end at $A$ and $C$, so both stand on the highlighted arc $AC$.

spec.description: Horizontal diameter AC with centre B, chords AE, EC and ED; ED crosses AC to the right of B. Upper semicircle AC through D highlighted.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABC is a straight central angle and angle AEC is at the circumference. Both stand on the highlighted semicircular arc AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; angle names are withheld.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC$ is the straight angle at the centre and $\angle AEC$ is at the circumference. Both stand on the highlighted semicircular arc $AC$.
